search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting measles cases, deaths, hospitalizations, dates, and subnational locations in Texas for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-30. Prioritize Texas DSHS official surveillance pages, CDC national measles tracking, WHO/PAHO situation reports, and high-quality news coverage that cites official figures.
search_reasoning: The upstream plan contains 10 queries across 5 channels but uses overly rigid quoted-phrase constructions (e.g., "measles Texas 2025" as a literal phrase) that may suppress relevant results. The plan also does not target the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) or CDC by name, which are the primary authoritative sources for Texas measles surveillance. Given the 4-query cap for this iteration, I prioritize: (1) Texas DSHS official surveillance — highest authority for subnational case counts; (2) CDC national measles tracking — cross-validates Texas figures and provides confirmed/probable breakdowns; (3) WHO/PAHO international situation reports — validates US/Texas data and may include death counts; (4) News/media search — captures outbreak announcements, locality detail, and hospitalization figures that official dashboards may lag. Quoted-phrase constraints are relaxed to improve recall. Time-scoping terms (2025, January–April) are embedded naturally. The 4 queries map to the 4 highest-priority source types and stay within the per-iteration cap.

query_batch.query: Texas measles cases 2025 DSHS site:dshs.texas.gov OR site:gov
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) directly — the primary subnational authority for Texas measles surveillance. Using site: operator to surface DSHS pages and other .gov domains. Avoids rigid quoted-phrase to improve recall. Expected to return DSHS measles dashboard, press releases, and situation updates with confirmed/probable case counts, death counts, and county-level breakdowns.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Texas DSHS measles surveillance page, DSHS press releases, Texas Health and Human Services measles updates
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official .gov domain; DSHS authorship; dated situation reports or dashboards

query_batch.query: CDC measles outbreak Texas 2025 cases deaths confirmed site:cdc.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets CDC.gov directly for national measles surveillance data that includes Texas state-level breakdowns. CDC publishes weekly measles case counts by state, MMWR outbreak investigation reports, and health advisory notices. The site: operator ensures results come from the authoritative federal source. Expected to yield confirmed/probable case counts, death data, and case classification details.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC measles cases and outbreaks page, MMWR reports, CDC health advisories referencing Texas 2025
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official CDC.gov domain; MMWR publication; dated surveillance tables

query_batch.query: measles outbreak Texas 2025 cases deaths hospitalizations WHO PAHO situation report
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets WHO and PAHO situation reports that may reference the Texas/US measles outbreak for international surveillance purposes. These reports often include cumulative case and death counts, age distributions, and vaccination coverage context. Useful as a cross-validation layer against DSHS and CDC figures, and may contain data not yet reflected in national dashboards.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO Disease Outbreak News, PAHO epidemiological alerts, WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record entries referencing US/Texas measles 2025
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: WHO.int or PAHO.org domain; dated situation report with case count tables

query_batch.query: Texas measles outbreak 2025 confirmed cases deaths county hospitalizations
query_batch.query_rationale: Broad news search to capture outbreak announcements, locality-level detail (county names, school or community clusters), hospitalization figures, and death reports that may precede or supplement official dashboard updates. News sources often cite DSHS or CDC figures directly and provide dated evidence quotes. Relaxed phrasing (no rigid quoted phrase) maximizes recall across AP, Reuters, Texas Tribune, local TV affiliates, and health news outlets.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: AP, Reuters, Texas Tribune, local Texas TV/newspaper outlets, ProPublica, Stat News — articles citing DSHS or CDC figures
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Named journalist byline; direct citation of DSHS or CDC spokesperson or data; dateline within Jan–Apr 2025

expected_evidence: Cumulative confirmed and probable measles case counts for Texas, Jan–Apr 2025
Death counts attributed to measles in Texas during the window
Specific county or locality names associated with cases
Dates of case onset or report dates
Official DSHS press releases or situation reports
CDC MMWR reports or outbreak investigation notices
WHO/PAHO situation report entries referencing Texas or the United States
expected_source_characteristics: Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) official website — primary subnational authority
CDC official measles surveillance pages or MMWR — national authority with state-level breakdowns
WHO or PAHO situation reports — international validation layer
Established news outlets (AP, Reuters, Texas Tribune, local TV affiliates) citing official figures — useful for locality detail and hospitalization data
language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. Texas public health reporting is conducted in English by DSHS. Spanish-language sources are not expected to be primary authorities for official case counts, though they may provide community-level context; this is deferred to iteration 2 if locality coverage is insufficient.
trust_considerations: Prefer sources that cite case counts directly from DSHS or CDC rather than secondary aggregators
Distinguish confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected case classifications
Note whether death figures are laboratory-confirmed measles deaths or clinically attributed
Be alert to cumulative vs. new-period case counts in dashboards
News sources are acceptable for locality and hospitalization detail only when they quote official figures
stop_condition_hypothesis: Iteration 1 is insufficient on its own; a second iteration will be needed to follow up on specific outbreak localities (e.g., Gaines County, West Texas communities) and to query structured databases (CDC NNDSS, HealthData.gov) if official dashboards do not surface granular case-level data.
warnings: Upstream quoted-phrase queries (e.g., exact string 'measles Texas 2025') may have low recall — relaxed phrasing used in this iteration
Texas DSHS may publish data under 'Rubeola' (the clinical synonym) rather than 'measles' in some official documents — rubeola term included in one query
The 2025 Texas measles outbreak was centered in West Texas / Gaines County area; locality-specific queries are deferred to iteration 2 pending confirmation from iteration 1 results
Peer-reviewed literature is unlikely to be available for a Jan–Apr 2025 outbreak within the same calendar year; literature channel deprioritized to iteration 2

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 produced strong foundational coverage from CDC MMWR, Texas DSHS, and Wikipedia, confirming the outbreak's existence, key localities (Gaines County, West Texas/South Plains, Harris County), and partial case/death/hospitalization figures. However, several critical gaps remain for the Jan–Apr 2025 window: (1) The DSHS main outbreak page (dshs.texas.gov/news-alerts/measles-outbreak-2025) references specific dated press releases (Feb 26 first death, Apr 6 second death) that were not individually surfaced as candidates — these are the primary authoritative sources for death counts within the task window; (2) The DSHS Jan 2025 Harris County alert mentions only 2 cases, while the outbreak page references a much larger cumulative count — intermediate DSHS press releases covering March and April 2025 case milestones are missing; (3) The April 6 second death announcement and April 7 expanded outbreak counties health alert are directly within the task window and not yet captured as discrete source candidates; (4) CDC's national measles case count tracker (separate from MMWR) and any DSHS weekly situation report updates for March–April 2025 have not been surfaced; (5) News coverage from Texas Tribune, local Lubbock/West Texas outlets, and AP/Reuters for the Feb–Apr 2025 period (covering the death announcements and case escalation) is underrepresented — only 1 Texas Tribune result appeared. A second iteration targeting these specific gaps will materially improve coverage of deaths, locality detail, and dated case milestones within the task window.

query_batch.query: DSHS Texas measles outbreak death February April 2025 press release site:dshs.texas.gov
query_batch.query_rationale: Directly targets the two DSHS death announcement press releases referenced in the DSHS outbreak page snippet: 'Feb. 26 Texas Announces First Death in Measles Outbreak' and 'April 6 Texas Announces Second Death in Measles Outbreak'. These are the primary authoritative sources for death counts within the task window and must be captured as discrete source candidates. Also expected to surface the April 7 DSHS Health Alert on expanded outbreak counties. Site-limiting to dshs.texas.gov maximizes precision.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: DSHS press releases dated Feb 26 2025 and Apr 6 2025 announcing measles deaths; DSHS Health Alert dated Apr 7 2025 on expanded outbreak counties
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official dshs.texas.gov domain; dated press release with death count and locality (Lubbock/Gaines County area)
query_batch.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q1 — DSHS outbreak page snippet referenced Feb 26 and Apr 6 death press releases not yet captured as discrete candidates

query_batch.query: CDC measles cases 2025 United States state count Texas tracker weekly
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets the CDC national measles case count surveillance table (distinct from MMWR outbreak reports), which tracks confirmed and probable cases by state on a weekly or cumulative basis. This page would provide a cross-validated Texas case count for the full Jan–Apr 2025 window, including any cases not associated with the West Texas outbreak cluster. The MMWR reports cover specific sub-periods; the national tracker covers the full window.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC 'Measles Cases and Outbreaks' surveillance page with state-level case count table for 2025; CDC health advisory or situation update referencing Texas cumulative totals
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official cdc.gov domain; dated surveillance table with state-level confirmed/probable case counts
query_batch.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q2 — CDC MMWR reports surfaced but national case count tracker page not yet identified as a discrete candidate

query_batch.query: Texas measles death child Lubbock 2025 Gaines County outbreak cases April
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets news coverage of the two child deaths in Lubbock referenced in the Wikipedia snippet, and the broader April 2025 case escalation. Local outlets (Lubbock Avalanche-Journal, KCBD, Plainview Herald) and wire services (AP, Reuters) would have covered the death announcements with dated evidence quotes, locality detail, and cumulative case counts at time of publication. This fills the news coverage gap for the Feb–Apr 2025 sub-period and provides corroborating evidence quotes for the death and hospitalization fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: AP or Reuters wire stories on Texas measles deaths; Lubbock Avalanche-Journal or KCBD local coverage; Texas Tribune follow-up articles citing DSHS figures for April 2025
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Named journalist byline; direct citation of DSHS spokesperson or official case count; dateline Feb–Apr 2025
query_batch.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q4 — news search returned only 1 Texas Tribune result; death announcement coverage and local outlet reporting not yet captured

query_batch.query: Texas measles 2025 Mennonite community cases not associated West Texas outbreak Harris County update
query_batch.query_rationale: The DSHS outbreak page snippet references '2025 Texas Measles Cases Not Associated with the Outbreak in West Texas' as a distinct category, and the Harris County DSHS alert (2 confirmed cases, January 2025) represents a separate cluster. The Wikipedia snippet identifies the Mennonite community as the primary affected group. This query targets coverage of non-West-Texas Texas cases (e.g., Harris County, other urban counties) and any DSHS updates distinguishing outbreak-associated vs. non-outbreak cases — important for accurate subnational_location and locality field population across the full task window.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: DSHS pages or news articles distinguishing West Texas outbreak cases from sporadic Texas cases; Harris County Public Health updates; coverage of Mennonite community context
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: DSHS or county health department authorship; dated update within Jan–Apr 2025 window; explicit case count breakdown by cluster
query_batch.previous_iteration_basis: iter1_q1 — DSHS outbreak page references non-West-Texas cases as a distinct category; Harris County alert surfaced but broader non-outbreak case coverage not yet captured

warnings: The DSHS main outbreak page (dshs.texas.gov/news-alerts/measles-outbreak-2025) was last updated Aug 12 2025 and references the full outbreak arc — when fetched, care must be taken to extract only data points with dates falling within the Jan 1–Apr 30 2025 task window.
The two child deaths in Lubbock referenced in the Wikipedia snippet should be verified against DSHS press releases — Wikipedia is not a primary source for death counts or dates.

The April 15 Texas Children's Hospital snapshot (561 cases) is within the task window but is a hospital page citing DSHS — the underlying DSHS figure should be cross-validated against the DSHS outbreak page.

CDC MMWR mm7520a1 covers Jan 20–Mar 18 2025 (325 cases, 1 death, 60 hospitalizations) — this is a sub-period report; the full Jan–Apr 2025 window will have higher cumulative totals that must be sourced from the DSHS outbreak page or CDC national tracker.
Iteration 2 is the final permitted iteration under the max_iterations: 2 bound — all remaining high-priority gaps must be addressed in this batch.
